title: Graphing with Software and Function Modeling
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Viewing Window and Graphical Resolution
definitions.statement: The rectangular display window of a computer graphics screen or graphing calculator defined by horizontal bounds [x_min, x_max] and vertical bounds [y_min, y_max].
conditions: Aspect ratio (scale ratio between x and y units) determines geometric distortion
definitions.explanation: Selecting an inappropriate window can hide significant local extrema, global behavior, or vertical asymptotes, or falsely suggest false features.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Choose viewing windows that capture all intercepts, turning points, and asymptotic trends.

definitions.title: Grapher Artifacts and Rapid Oscillations
definitions.statement: Digital graphing utilities sample a finite grid of pixels. When a function oscillates faster than the pixel sampling rate (aliasing), or near vertical asymptotes, graphers can display erratic or spurious lines.
conditions: Sampling rate Nyquist limit applies to digital rendering
Discontinuities may appear erroneously connected by vertical segments
definitions.explanation: Analytic analysis must always accompany machine plotting to prevent misinterpreting sampling artifacts as genuine mathematical behavior.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Never rely solely on digital plots without algebraic verification of limits and singularities.

definitions.title: Parametric Curve in the Coordinate Plane
definitions.latex: x = f(t), \quad y = g(t), \quad t \in I
definitions.statement: If x and y are continuous functions of a third variable t (the parameter) defined on an interval I, the set of points (x, y) = (f(t), g(t)) forms a parametric curve in the coordinate plane.
conditions: Parameter t frequently represents time, orientation, or angle
Curves trace out a definite direction of motion as t increases
definitions.explanation: Parametric equations generalize functional curves, allowing curves that fail the vertical line test (e.g. self-intersecting loops and circles) to be represented algebraically.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Parametric equations describe both the path of motion and the time/direction of traversal.

definitions.title: Eliminating the Parameter
definitions.latex: x = r\cos t, \ y = r\sin t \implies x^2 + y^2 = r^2
definitions.statement: The process of solving one parametric equation for t (or applying a trigonometric/algebraic identity) to derive an equivalent Cartesian relation in x and y.
conditions: Care must be taken to retain the domain and range restrictions imposed by the original parameter interval
definitions.explanation: Eliminating t reveals the underlying geometric shape while verifying that the parametric trajectory covers all or part of the Cartesian curve.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Apply identities like cos^2(t) + sin^2(t) = 1 to eliminate circular trigonometric parameters.

definitions.title: Empirical Mathematical Modeling
definitions.statement: The process of fitting functional equations to experimentally measured data sets using regression, log-log transformations, or semi-log transformations.
conditions: Semi-log plot (log y vs x) linearizes exponential growth
Log-log plot (log y vs log x) linearizes power-law models
definitions.explanation: Logarithmic transformations convert non-linear power and exponential laws into linear forms, facilitating parameter estimation.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Log-log lines represent power functions; semi-log lines represent exponential functions.
